passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: According to the Yavanas a person born when three or more malefic planets are in their exaltation signs becomes a tyrannical king (a). According to Jeevasarma if such planets be malefic a person will never become a king (b).
passages.summary: According to the Yavanas, a person born when three or more malefic planets are in their signs of exaltation becomes a tyrannical king. According to Jeevasarma, if those planets are malefic the person will never become a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: (a). If three or more planets occupying their exaltation signs be benefic, the person becomes a good king;
passages.summary: The translator's note says that if three or more planets in their signs of exaltation are benefic, the person becomes a good king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: if [three or more planets occupying their exaltation signs be] both benefic and malefic he will become both a good and a bad king,
passages.summary: The translator's note says that if the three or more exalted planets are a mix of benefic and malefic, the person becomes both a good and a bad king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: (b). According to Jeevasarma, such a person becomes rich and powerful but not a king. Varaha Mihira is of the opinion of the Yavanas.
passages.summary: The translator's note says that according to Jeevasarma such a person becomes rich and powerful but not a king, and that Varaha Mihira sides with the Yavanas.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Of the four planets, Mars, Saturn, the Sun, and Jupiter, by all the four or any three of them occupying exaltation signs while each of the planets occupies the Lagna, the number of Rajayogas is 16.
passages.summary: The text counts 16 Rajayogas formed when all four, or any three, of Mars, Saturn, the Sun and Jupiter are in their exaltation signs with one of them in the ascendant. It only counts the yogas.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, of the same four planets by any two or by any one occupying exaltation signs and in each case by each of the planets occupying the Lagna while the Moon occupies sign Cancer, the number of Rajayogas is also 16.
passages.summary: The text counts another 16 Rajayogas formed when any two, or any one, of the same four planets are exalted with one of them in the ascendant while the Moon is in Cancer. It only counts the yogas.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: 32 Rajayogas are mentioned in this stanza. A person born under any one of them becomes a king : suppose all the 4 planets— Mars, Saturn, the Sun and Jupiter — to occupy their exaltation signs at the same time; by any one of such signs being the ascendant the number of Rajayogas obtained is 4. Again, of the same 4 planets there are 4 groups, each of three planets, thus (1) Mars, Saturn and the Sun, (2) Mars, Saturn and Jupiter, (3) Mars, the Sun and Jupiter, (4) Saturn, the Sun and Jupiter. In the case of each group, by all the three planets occupying their exaltation signs and by each of such signs being the rising sign, the number of Rajayogas obtained is 3; there being 4 such groups the number of Rajayogas obtained from them all is 4X3 or 12. Adding this to the 4 yogas already obtained we get the first 16 yogas mentioned in the text.
passages.summary: The translator's note says a person born under any of the 32 Rajayogas becomes a king, and works out the first 16: 4 from all four planets exalted plus 12 from the four groups of three.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, of the same 4 planets, there are 6 groups each of 2 planets as follows (1) Mars and Saturn, (2) Mars and the Sun, (3) Mars and Jupiter, (4) Saturn and the Sun, (5) Saturn and Jupiter and (6) the Sun and Jupiter. In the case of each group by both the planets occupying their exaltation signs and by each of such signs being the rising sign, the number of Rajayogas obtained is 2. There being 6 such groups, the number of yogas obtained from them all is 6X2 or 12. In each of these 12 cases, the Moon occupies sign Cancer. Again, of the same 4 planets, by their severally being in their exaltation signs, while such sign is also the rising sign, the number of Rajayogas obtained is 4. In each of these 4 cases, the Moon occupies sign Cancer. Adding these 4 yogas to the 12 yogas already obtained we get the second 16 yogas mentioned in the text.
passages.summary: The translator's note works out the second 16 Rajayogas: 12 from the six pairs of planets and 4 from single planets, each with the Moon in Cancer. It only counts the yogas.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: The Lagna or the Moon being in Vargottama positions, of all the planets, excepting the Moon, by the several groups of four, five and six planets aspecting the Lagna or the Moon, the number of yogas obtained is 22.
passages.summary: The text counts 22 yogas formed when the ascendant or the Moon is in a Vargottama position and is aspected by groups of four, five or six of the other planets. It only counts the yogas.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text:
The six planets are, the Sun, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn. Of these there are 15 groups each of 4 planets as follows :

All the 6 planets form again into one group. Thus there are 22 groups. By the planets of each group aspecting the rising sign in its Vargothama position, the number of yogas obtained is 22; and by their aspecting the Moon in its Vargothama position, the number of yogas obtained is again 22. According to Mandavya, by each of the 12 signs from Aries being either the rising sign or the sign occupied by the Moon in the case of each yoga, the number of yogas obtained is 44X12 or 528.
passages.summary: The translator's note lists the 15 groups of four planets, 6 groups of five and 1 group of six, giving 22 yogas for the ascendant and 22 for the Moon. According to Mandavya, counting each of the 12 signs gives 528 yogas. It only counts the yogas.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Saturn occupies sign Aquarius, the Sun sign Aries, the Moon sign Taurus, Mercury sign Gemini, Jupiter sign Leo, and Mars sign Scorpio, a person born becomes a king when the rising sign is Aquarius or when it is Aries or when it is Taurus.
passages.summary: The text says that with Saturn in Aquarius, the Sun in Aries, the Moon in Taurus, Mercury in Gemini, Jupiter in Leo and Mars in Scorpio, a person born with Aquarius, Aries or Taurus rising becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, when Saturn occupies sign Libra, the Moon sign Taurus, the Sun and Mercury sign Virgo, Venus sign Libra, Mars sign Aries, and Jupiter sign Cancer, a person born becomes a king when the rising sign is Libra or when it is Taurus.
passages.summary: The text says that with Saturn in Libra, the Moon in Taurus, the Sun and Mercury in Virgo, Venus in Libra, Mars in Aries and Jupiter in Cancer, a person born with Libra or Taurus rising becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Mars occupies sign Capricorn, the Sun and the Moon sign Sagittari, Saturn sign Capricorn and when the rising sign is also Capricorn, a person born becomes a king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Mars in Capricorn, the Sun and Moon in Sagittarius, Saturn in Capricorn and Capricorn rising, a person born becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again when the rising sign is Capricorn and when Mars and the Moon occupy it, and when the Sun occupies sign Sagittari, a person born becomes a king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Capricorn rising and holding Mars and the Moon, and the Sun in Sagittarius, a person born becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again when Aries is the rising sign and when the Sun occupies it, when Saturn and the Moon occupy sign Libra and Jupiter occupies sign Sagittari, a person becomes a king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Aries rising and holding the Sun, Saturn and the Moon in Libra, and Jupiter in Sagittarius, a person becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When the rising sign is Taurus and the Moon occupies it, when the Sun occupies sign Leo, Jupiter sign Scorpio and Saturn sign Aquarius a person born becomes a king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Taurus rising and holding the Moon, the Sun in Leo, Jupiter in Scorpio and Saturn in Aquarius, a person born becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, when the rising sign is Capricorn, and when Saturn occupies it, and when the Moon occupies the 3rd house, Mars the 6th house, Mercury the 9th house, and Jupiter the 12th house, a person born becomes a virtuous and famous king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Capricorn rising and holding Saturn, the Moon in the 3rd house, Mars in the 6th, Mercury in the 9th and Jupiter in the 12th, a person born becomes a virtuous and famous king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When the Moon and Jupiter occupy sign Sagittari, and when Mars occupies the first half of Capricorn, a person born becomes a king when Pisces is the rising sign and Venus occupies it or when Virgo is rising sign and Mercury occupies it.
passages.summary: The text says that with the Moon and Jupiter in Sagittarius and Mars in the first half of Capricorn, a person born becomes a king if Pisces rises holding Venus or Virgo rises holding Mercury.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, when the rising sign is Virgo and when Mercury occupies it, when Mars and Saturn occupy the 5th house, when the Moon, Jupiter and Venus occupy the 4th house, a person born becomes a king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Virgo rising and holding Mercury, Mars and Saturn in the 5th house, and the Moon, Jupiter and Venus in the 4th house, a person born becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Pisces is the rising sign, and the Moon occupies it, and when Aquarius, Capricorn and Leo are respectively occupied by Saturn, Mars, and the Sun, a person born becomes a king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Pisces rising and holding the Moon, Saturn in Aquarius, Mars in Capricorn and the Sun in Leo, a person born becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, when Mars occupies sign Aries and Jupiter sign Cancer, a person born becomes a king when Aries is the rising sign, also when Cancer is the rising sign.
passages.summary: The text says that with Mars in Aries and Jupiter in Cancer, a person born with Aries or Cancer rising becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Cancer is the rising sign and Jupiter occupies it, and when the Moon, Venus and Mercury occupy sign Taurus and the Sun sign Aries, a person born becomes a powerful king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Cancer rising and holding Jupiter, the Moon, Venus and Mercury in Taurus, and the Sun in Aries, a person born becomes a powerful king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Capricorn is the rising sign and Saturn occupies it, when the signs Aries, Cancer and Leo are occupied by their lords and when Gemini and Libra are respectively occupied by Mercury and Venus, a person born becomes a famous king.
passages.summary: The text says that with Capricorn rising and holding Saturn, Aries, Cancer and Leo each holding their own lords, Mercury in Gemini and Venus in Libra, a person born becomes a famous king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Virgo is the rising sign, and Mercury occupies it, when Venus occupies sign Gemini, the Moon and Jupiter occupy sign Pisces, and Mars and Saturn occupy sign Capricorn, a person born becomes a King.
passages.summary: The text says that with Virgo rising and holding Mercury, Venus in Gemini, the Moon and Jupiter in Pisces, and Mars and Saturn in Capricorn, a person born becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Persons born under the various yogas described above, though they may be born in low families will become kings. If such persons are born in a king's family they will doubtless become kings. We shall now proceed to describe certain yogas, persons born under which will become kings if they belong to a king's family and will become rich if otherwise.
passages.summary: The text says that people born under the yogas described so far become kings whatever family they are born into. It announces that the yogas that follow make a person a king only if born into a royal family, and otherwise rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When three or more planets are powerful and occupy either their houses or Exaltation signs or their Moolatrikona signs, a person born becomes a king if he belongs to a king's family.
passages.summary: The text says that when three or more planets are strong and placed in their own, exaltation or Moolatrikona signs, a person born into a royal family becomes a king.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, when five or more planets are powerful and occupy their houses or exaltation signs or their Moolatrikona signs a person born becomes a king even if he be born in a low family.
passages.summary: The text says that when five or more planets are strong and placed in their own, exaltation or Moolatrikona signs, a person becomes a king even if born into a low family.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: If in either case, the number of powerful planets be less than three or five, the persons described above will not become kings but will become only rich.
passages.summary: The text says that if the number of such strong planets falls short of three or five respectively, the person does not become a king but only becomes rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Aries is the rising sign and the Sun and Moon occupy it, when Mars occupies sign Capricorn, Saturn sign Aquarius, and Jupiter sign Sagittari, a person born becomes a king, if he belong to a king's family, and will become only rich if otherwise.
passages.summary: The text says that with Aries rising and holding the Sun and Moon, Mars in Capricorn, Saturn in Aquarius and Jupiter in Sagittarius, a person of royal family becomes a king, and otherwise only rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: According to another reading, the Sun is made to occupy sign Leo and the yoga remains the same in other respects.
passages.summary: The translator's note says that another reading of the text places the Sun in Leo, with the rest of the yoga unchanged.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Venus occupies the 4th house, and when such house is his own, when the Moon occupies the 9th house, and when the other planets occupy the 3rd, 1st and 11th houses, a person born becomes a king, if he belong to a king's family and only rich if otherwise.
passages.summary: The text says that with Venus in the 4th house in his own sign, the Moon in the 9th house and the other planets in the 3rd, 1st and 11th houses, a person of royal family becomes a king, and otherwise only rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: As Venus is said to be in his Swakshetra he might be either in sign Taurus or in sign Libra. The Lagna must therefore be either sign Aquarius or sign Cancer respectively. As the Moon is said to be in the 9th house, he occupies sign Libra in the former case, and sign Pisces in the latter, and as the other planets are said to occupy the 3rd, 1st and 11th houses from Lagna, these houses are signs Aries, Aquarius and Sagittari in the one case, and Virgo, Cancer and Taurus in the other. Thus 2 yogas are referred to in this stanza.
passages.summary: The translator's note works out that Venus in his own sign in the 4th means either Taurus with Aquarius rising or Libra with Cancer rising, and gives the signs for the Moon and the other planets in each case, so the verse describes two yogas.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Mercury is powerful and occupies the rising sign, (a) when a benefic planet (b) occupies the 9th house (c) and when the other planets (d) occupy the 9th, 2nd, 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th houses (e), a person born becomes a virtuous king if he belong to a king's family and only rich if otherwise.
passages.notes:
(a). This may be any one of the 12 signs.
(b). This is either Jupiter or Venus.
(d). When one or more of the other planets according to commentator.
(e). One of these houses according to commentator.
passages.summary: The text says that with a strong Mercury in the ascendant, a benefic in the 9th house and the other planets in the 9th, 2nd, 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th houses, a person of royal family becomes a virtuous king, and otherwise only rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: (c). The 4th house according to a different reading.
passages.summary: The translator's note says that a different reading places the benefic planet in the 4th house instead of the 9th.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Taurus is the rising sign, and the Moon occupies it, when Jupiter occupies the 2nd house, Saturn the 6th house, and the other planets the 11th house, a person born becomes a king if he belong to a king's family, and only rich if otherwise.
passages.summary: The text says that with Taurus rising and holding the Moon, Jupiter in the 2nd house, Saturn in the 6th and the other planets in the 11th, a person of royal family becomes a king, and otherwise only rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, when Jupiter occupies the 4th house, the Sun and the Moon occupy the 10th house, when Saturn occupies the Lagna (a) and when the other planets occupy the 11th house, a person born becomes a king if he be born in a king's family, and only rich if otherwise.
passages.notes: (a.) This may be any one of the 12 signs according to commentator.
passages.summary: The text says that with Jupiter in the 4th house, the Sun and Moon in the 10th, Saturn in the ascendant and the other planets in the 11th, a person of royal family becomes a king, and otherwise only rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When the Moon occupies the 10th house, Saturn the 11th house, Jupiter the rising sign, Mercury and Mars the 2nd house, and the Sun and Venus occupy the 4th house, a person born becomes a king if he belong to a king's family, and only rich if otherwise.
passages.summary: The text says that with the Moon in the 10th house, Saturn in the 11th, Jupiter in the ascendant, Mercury and Mars in the 2nd, and the Sun and Venus in the 4th, a person of royal family becomes a king, and otherwise only rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, when Mars and Saturn occupy the rising sign, when the Moon occupies the 4th house, Jupiter the 7th house, Venus the 9th house, the Sun the 10th house, and Mercury the 11th house, a person born becomes a king if he belong to a king's family, and only rich if otherwise.
passages.summary: The text says that with Mars and Saturn in the ascendant, the Moon in the 4th house, Jupiter in the 7th, Venus in the 9th, the Sun in the 10th and Mercury in the 11th, a person of royal family becomes a king, and otherwise only rich.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Of the planets producing a Rajayoga either in the Antardasa periods of those which occupy the 10th house or the Lagna (a) or in that of the most powerful planet (b), a person obtains kingdom and he loses it and courts the friendship of another king in the Antardasa periods of the planets occupying inimical or depression signs (c).
passages.notes:
(a). If there be planets both in the Lagna and in the 10th house or if there be several planets in either, then in the Antardasa period of the most powerful of them.
(b). If there be no planets both in Lagna and in the 10th house.
passages.summary: The text says that a person gains a kingdom during the sub-periods of the Rajayoga planets placed in the 10th house or the ascendant, or else of the strongest planet. He loses it and seeks the friendship of another king during the sub-periods of planets in enemy or debilitation signs.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: (c). If such planets be powerful the king will lose his kingdom permanently, and if they be not powerful, he will recover it by the help of his allies.
passages.summary: The translator's note says that if those planets are strong the king loses his kingdom permanently, and if they are weak he recovers it with the help of allies.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: When Jupiter, Venus and Mercury occupy the rising sign, (a) when Saturn occupies the 7th house and the Sun the 10th house, a person born will live in great comfort and luxury, (b)
passages.notes: (b). Though he may be poor.
passages.summary: The text says that with Jupiter, Venus and Mercury in the ascendant, Saturn in the 7th house and the Sun in the 10th, a person born will live in great comfort and luxury.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: Again, when powerful benefic signs form the Kendras and malefic planets occupy malefic signs, a person born becomes rich and the chief of hunters and robbers.
passages.summary: The text says that when strong benefic signs form the angular houses and malefic planets are in malefic signs, a person born becomes rich and the chief of hunters and robbers.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: (a). The rising sign is Aries according to commentator. The interpretation given of this portion of the text is objected to by some on the ground that when Venus and Mercury (the inferior planets) occupy the rising sign the Sun cannot occupy the 10th house — a place more than 60 degrees removed from them. For the greatest elongations of the two planets from the Sun are respectively 47 and 29 degrees. Accordingly the following interpretation is proposed:— "If the rising sign be the house of Jupiter, Venus or Mercury" Bhatta Utpala, the commentator, while granting the validity of the objection, says, that the interpretation objected to has the support of Garga whom he quotes. A similar remark applies to the Vajra and other yogas described in stanza 5 of the next Chapter, and in stanza 6 of the same, Varaha Mihira while admitting the impossibility of the yoga, says that his task is simply to state the views of the ancient writers and nothing more. Vide notes to stanza 6, Chapter XII.
passages.summary: The translator's note says the commentator takes the rising sign as Aries, and that some object the Sun cannot be in the 10th house when Venus and Mercury are in the ascendant, proposing instead a rising sign ruled by Jupiter, Venus or Mercury. The commentator Bhatta Utpala grants the objection but cites Garga in support of the original reading, and Varaha Mihira says he only records the views of ancient writers.

passages.chapterTitle: On Raja Yoga, or the Birth of Kings
passages.text: (c). This portion of the text is interpreted by some as follows : "When powerful benefic planets occupy the Kendras" But this interpretation is opposed to Garga whom the commentator quotes.
passages.summary: The translator's note says some read this condition as strong benefic planets occupying the angular houses, but that this reading goes against Garga, whom the commentator quotes.

passages.text: Nine, ten and eight multiplied respectively by three, three and four give the sums of the numbers of the first two, the first three, and all the four groups of Nabhasa yogas (a). The Yavanas treat extensively of one thousand and eight hundred of such yogas (b). We shall here summarize them.
passages.notes:
(b). Vide note at the end of the Chapter for the particulars of the 1800 Nabhasa yogas.
(c). The author says that his 32 yogas contain the 1800 yogas of the Yavanas.
passages.summary: The text gives the number of Nabhasa yogas in four groups as running totals stated through multiplication. It says the Yavanas discuss 1,800 such yogas and that the author will summarize them. The record only counts and classifies yogas.

passages.text: (a). Curiously enough the author adopts a rather circuitous method of stating the numbers of the several groups of Nabhasa yogas. The statement amounts to an Algebraical problem : find 4 numbers such that the 1st + the 2nd=9x3=27. 1st+2nd+3rd=10x3=30. 1st+2nd+3rd+4th=8x4=32. It is clear that the number of the last group =32—30=2. The number of the 3rd group=30—27=3. The number of the first and second group is given as 27. According to the commentator, the 1st group consists of 20 yogas and the 2nd of 7. In other words what the author wants to say is briefly this — The Nabhasa yogas consist of 4 groups as follows : Akriti yogas 20 ; Sankhya yogas 7 ; Asraya yogas 3 ; and Dala yogas 2.
passages.summary: The translator's note works out the verse's arithmetic. Following the commentator, it concludes there are 20 Akriti, 7 Sankhya, 3 Asraya and 2 Dala yogas. It only counts and classifies yogas.

passages.text: According to Satyachariyar if all the planets occupy (a) the movable, fixed or common signs, the yogas are respectively known as Rajju, Musala, and Nala, and these three form the group of Asraya yogas.
passages.notes: (a). One or two or three or all the four of the signs. According to some the planets ought to occupy all the four signs. This is opposed to Garga.
passages.summary: According to Satyacharya, as the text reports, the yogas are called Rajju, Musala and Nala when all the planets are in movable, fixed or common signs respectively. These three make up the Asraya group.

passages.text: Again according to Parasara, if the benefic planets (b) occupy the Kendras (c) the yoga is known as Srik or Mala;
passages.notes:
(b). Viz., Mercury, Jupiter and Venus according to Garga.
(c). Three of the Kendras, while there are no malefic planets in any of the kendra houses according to Badarayana.
passages.summary: According to Parasara, as the text reports, the yoga is called Srik or Mala when the benefic planets occupy the angular houses. The notes identify the benefics as Mercury, Jupiter and Venus.

passages.text: [Again according to Parasara,] and if malefic planets (d) occupy the Kendras (e) the yoga is known as Sarpa. These two form the group of Dala yogas.
passages.notes:
(d). Viz. :— The Sun, Mars and Saturn according to Garga.
(e). Three of the kendras, while there are no benefic planets in any of the kendra houses according to Badarayana.
passages.summary: According to Parasara, as the text reports, the yoga is called Sarpa when the malefic planets occupy the angular houses. The notes identify the malefics as the Sun, Mars and Saturn. Mala and Sarpa together form the Dala group.

passages.text: Other Astrologers say that the Asraya yogas are identical with the Yava (a), Abja (b), Vajra (c), Andaja (d), Gola (e), and the like yogas (f), and that when the effects of planets occupying the kendras are described the effects of Dala yogas are also described and they produce no separate effects (g).
passages.notes:
In this stanza the author explains the reason why certain Astrologers have failed to treat of the Asraya and Dala yogas in their works.
(a), (b), (c). Vide stanza 5.
(d). Vide stanza 4.
(e). Vide stanza 10.
(f). The like yogas : such as Sakata (stanza 4), Kedara, Sula and Yuga (all stanza 10).
The Asraya yogas may be these and may not be these; hence the author has deemed it advisable to treat them separately. For instance, if all planets occupy signs Gemini and Sagittarius — 2 of the common signs — when one of these is also the rising sign, the yoga is known both as Vajra and Nala ; but if any other sign be the rising sign, it is not a Vajra yoga but only a Nala yoga.
(g). As regards the Dala yogas, it is said that other writers have described the effects of benefic and of malefic planets occupying the Kendras and as these are also the effects of the two Dala yogas they have omitted to treat of them separately ; the author treats of these separately in order to make it known that the two are Nabhasa yogas and as such their effects are felt throughout life (vide Stanza 19).
passages.summary: The text reports that other astrologers regard the Asraya yogas as identical with Yava, Abja, Vajra, Andaja, Gola and similar yogas. Those astrologers also hold that the Dala yogas have no separate effect beyond that of planets in the angular houses.

passages.text: If all the planets occupy any two adjacent Kendras, the yoga is known as Gada (a).
passages.notes:
The author now proceeds to describe the 20 Akriti yogas. 5 of them are described in this stanza.
(a). This may be in 4 ways : All the four planets may occupy (1), the 1st and the 4th houses, (2), the 4th and 7th houses (3), the 7th and the 10th houses and (4), the 10th and the 1st house. The Yavanas consider these 4 as four distinct yogas and call them respectively as Gada, Sankha, Vibhuka and Dwaja. (Vide note at the end of the Chapter.)
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Gada when all the planets occupy any two adjacent angular houses.

passages.text: If they all occupy the ascendant and the 7th house, the yoga is known as Sakata.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Sakata when all the planets occupy the ascendant and the 7th house.

passages.text: If all the planets occupy the 4th and the 10th house the yoga is known as Vihaga.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Vihaga when all the planets occupy the 4th and 10th houses.

passages.text: If all the planets occupy the ascendant, the 5th and 9th houses, the yoga is known as Sringataka
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Sringataka when all the planets occupy the ascendant, the 5th and the 9th houses.

passages.text: and if all the planets occupy other triangular houses the yoga is known as Hala (b).
passages.notes: (b). This may be in three ways : all the planets may occupy, (1), the 2nd, 6th and 10th houses, (2), the 3rd, 7th and 11th houses, (3) the 4th, 8th and 12th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Hala when all the planets occupy one of the other sets of mutually trinal houses that do not include the ascendant.

passages.text: If the benefic planets occupy the ascendant and the 7th house while the malefic planets occupy the 4th and 10th houses the Yoga is known as Vajra ;
passages.notes: In this stanza, 4 more Akriti yogas are described.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Vajra when the benefic planets occupy the ascendant and the 7th house while the malefic planets occupy the 4th and 10th houses.

passages.text: and if the reverse be the case (a) the yoga is known as Yava.
passages.notes: (a). That is if the malefic planets occupy the ascendant and the 7th house while the benefic planets occupy the 4th and 10th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Yava in the reverse case, with malefics in the ascendant and 7th house and benefics in the 4th and 10th houses.

passages.text: Again, if all the planets occupy the four Kendras the yoga is known as Kamala,
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Kamala when all the planets occupy the four angular houses.

passages.text: and if they occupy the four Panaphara (b) or the four Apoklima (c) houses, the yoga is known as Vapi.
passages.notes:
(b). That is the 2nd, 5th, 8th and 11th houses.
(c). That is the 3rd, 6th, 9th and 12th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Vapi when all the planets occupy the four succedent houses or the four cadent houses.

passages.text: I have described the Vajra and other (a) yogas adopting the view of former writers (b). How can Mercury and Venus occupy the 4th sign from the Sun?
passages.notes:
(a). That is the Yava yoga and the yoga mentioned in the beginning of stanza 20, of the Chapter on Rajayoga.
(b). Maya, Yavana, Garga and others.
passages.summary: The author says he has described Vajra and similar yogas following earlier writers. He questions how Mercury and Venus could ever be in the 4th sign from the Sun.

passages.text:
(c). According to Mr. Sundareswara Srouty of Trivadi, the Vajra and Yava yogas refer to the positions of the planets in the Bhava Chakra and not to their positions in their Rasi Chakra as supposed by Varaha Mihira. He is therefore of opinion that Garga and other writers have not erred in treating of these yogas as possible ones. This we shall now explain :
Varaha Mihira says "How can Mercury and Venus occupy the 4th sign from the Sun" The word used in the text is Bhavana which means a sign of the Zodiac (vide stanza 4, Chapter I). If the Vajra and Yava yogas refer to the positions of the planets in the Rasi Chakra then Varaha Mihira is right in declaring that the ancient writers have erred, but not if the yogas refer to the positions of the planets in the Bhava Chakra. Indeed in all yogas where the positions of the planets are stated with reference to particular Bhavas or houses from the ascendant, they refer to Bhava Chakra. As it is somewhat tedious to construct this Chakra (table), most of the astrologers confound it with the other Chakra and wrongly apply all yogas to the Rasi Chakra. This is one of fruitful sources of error in astrological predictions ; we shall now explain what is meant by Bhava Chakra. For the process of constructing it, the reader is referred to the Appendix at the end of the Book.
Both Rasi and Bhava Chakras are divisions of the ecliptic ; the former is division into 12 equal parts and the latter is division into 12 unequal parts depending upon the latitude of the place.
Bhaskara Charyar defines Bhava Chakra as follows in his Gola Adhyaya :
"The point where the ecliptic cuts the horizon in the east is known as eastern or rising Lagna, and in the west as the western or setting Lagna, and the points where the meridian of the place cuts the ecliptic are known as Madhya or middle Lagnas. — The 10th and 4th Lagnas."
These 4 points are respectively the middle points of the 1st, 7th, 10th and 4th Bhavas. The two points of trisection of the distance between the middle points of the 1st and 4th Bhavas are respectively the middle points of the 2nd and 3rd Bhavas. The two points of trisection of the distance between the middle points of the 4th and 7th Bhavas are respectively the middle points of the 5th and 6th Bhavas. The two points of trisection of the distance between middle points of the 7th and 10th Bhavas are the middle points of the 8th and 9th Bhavas. And the two points of trisection of the distance between the middle points of the 10th and 1st Bhavas are the middle points of the 11th and 12th Bhavas. Thus we have obtained the middle points of the 12 Bhavas. Now if we bisect these twelve divisions of the ecliptic, the space between the two points of bisection immediately on both sides of the middle point of each Bhava will form a Bhava.
Now as the ecliptic is inclined to the equator by about 23 degrees, the pole of the ecliptic will always be removed from the pole of the equator by about 23 degrees and will describe round it a circle in the course of each day. So that every day the plane of the ecliptic meridian will coincide with the plane of the meridian of the place twice. Now the point where the ecliptic meridian bisects the ecliptic is known in Astronomy as the nonagesimal point. Call this point N. Call the point where the meridian cuts the ecliptic M and the points where the horizon cuts the ecliptic in the east and west as E and W respectively.
So that N E = N W = 90 degrees = 3 signs, and M E is always 3 bhavas and M W is also 3 bhavas, M being the middle point of the 10th Bhava.
Now when the plane of the ecliptic meridian coincides with the plane of the meridian of the place, N coincides with M and therefore N M vanishes and the Rasi and Bhava Chakras coincide. This will occur twice a day. At other times they will differ. Now in the higher latitudes the angle between the two meridian lines increases. (Vide Spherical Trigonometry). Therefore the distance N M also increases and M W accordingly diminishes and it may even become less than 47 and 27 degrees and it nevertheless contains 3 bhavas. So that it is possible for Mercury and Venus to occupy M (the 10th bhava) while the Sun occupies W (the 7th bhava), i. e., Venus and Mercury may occupy the 4th bhava from the Sun. So that Garga and other writers have not erred if the Vajra and Yava yogas refer to the positions of the planets in the Bhava Chakra.
passages.summary: The translator's note reports Sundareswara Srouty's view that the Vajra and Yava yogas refer to house (Bhava) positions rather than sign positions. It explains how the house divisions are built and argues that by houses, Mercury and Venus can fall in the 4th house from the Sun. On that view, it says, Garga and the other earlier writers did not err.

passages.text: If all the planets occupy the four signs (a) from the ascendant, the yoga is known as Yupa;
passages.notes:
In this stanza the author describes four more Akriti yogas.
(a). That is the ascendant and the 2nd, 3rd and 4th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Yupa when all the planets occupy the four signs from the ascendant through the 4th house.

passages.text: if they occupy the four signs (b) from the fourth house, the yoga is known as Ishu or Bana ;
passages.notes: (b). That is the 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Ishu or Bana when all the planets occupy the four signs from the 4th house through the 7th.

passages.text: if they occupy the four signs (c) from the seventh house, the yoga is known as Sakti ;
passages.notes: (c). That is the 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Sakti when all the planets occupy the four signs from the 7th house through the 10th.

passages.text: and if they occupy the four signs (d) from the 10th house the yoga is known as Danda.
passages.notes: (d). That is the 10th, 11th and 12th houses and the ascendant.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Danda when all the planets occupy the four signs from the 10th house through the ascendant.

passages.text: If, as before, all the planets occupy the seven signs (a) from the ascendant the yoga is known as Nau ;
passages.notes:
In this stanza, the author describes 5 more Akriti yogas.
(a). That is, the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Nau when all the planets occupy the seven signs from the ascendant through the 7th house.

passages.text: if they occupy the seven signs (b) from the fourth house, the yoga is known as Kuta ;
passages.notes: (b). That is from the 4th to the 10th house.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Kuta when all the planets occupy the seven signs from the 4th house through the 10th.

passages.text: if they occupy the seven signs (c) from the seventh house, the yoga is known as Chhatra ;
passages.notes: (c). That is from the 7th to the 12th house and the ascendant.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Chhatra when all the planets occupy the seven signs from the 7th house through the ascendant.

passages.text: and if they occupy the seven signs (d) from the tenth house the yoga is known as Chapa.
passages.notes: (d). That is from the 10th to the 12th house and from the ascendant to the 4th house.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Chapa when all the planets occupy the seven signs from the 10th house through the 4th.

passages.text: Again if all the planets occupy the seven houses beginning from a Panaphara or Apoklima house, the yoga is known as Ardha-Chandra (e).
passages.notes: (e) As there are 4 Panaphara and 4 Apoklima houses the Ardha-Chandra yogas are of 8 kinds : viz., all the planets may occupy (1) from the 2nd to the 8th house, (2), from the 3rd to the 9th house, (3), from the 5th to the 11th house, (4), from the 6th to the 12th house, (5), from the 8th to the 2nd house, (6) from the 9th to the 3rd house, (7), from the 11th to the 5th house, (8), from the 12th to the 6th house.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Ardha-Chandra when all the planets occupy seven consecutive houses beginning from a succedent or cadent house.

passages.text: If the planets (a) occupy the six alternate signs (b) beginning from the 2nd house the yoga is known as Samudra,
passages.notes:
In this stanza the author describes the remaining 2 (out of 20) Akriti yogas.
(a). All the seven planets.
(b). That is, the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th and 12th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Samudra when all seven planets occupy the six alternate signs beginning from the 2nd house.

passages.text: and if they occupy the six alternate signs (c) beginning from ascendant the yoga is known as Chakra. Thus the Akriti yogas have been described briefly.
passages.notes: (c) That is the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th and 11th houses.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Chakra when all the planets occupy the six alternate signs beginning from the ascendant. This completes its brief description of the Akriti yogas.

passages.text: If all the planets occupy any seven signs the yoga is known as Vallaki ;
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Vallaki when all the planets occupy any seven signs.

passages.text: if they occupy any six signs, the yoga is known as Damini ;
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Damini when all the planets occupy any six signs.

passages.text: if they occupy any five signs it is known as Pasa;
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Pasa when all the planets occupy any five signs.

passages.text: if any four signs, it is known as Kedara ;
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Kedara when all the planets occupy any four signs.

passages.text: if any three signs it is known as Sula ;
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Sula when all the planets occupy any three signs.

passages.text: if any two signs, it is known as Yuga ;
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Yuga when all the planets occupy any two signs.

passages.text: and if they occupy a single sign, the yoga is known as Gola.
passages.summary: The text says the yoga is called Gola when all the planets occupy a single sign.

passages.text: When any of these Sankhya yogas are at the same time any other Nabhasa yogas, they are to be treated as belonging to the latter class (a).
passages.notes: (a). For instance the Gada, Sakata and Vihaga yogas described in stanza 4 are to be treated only as such and not as Yuga yogas described in this stanza ; the Sringataka and Hala yogas described in stanza 4 are to be treated only as such and not as Sula yogas described in this stanza. Again, the Vajra, Yava, Kamala and Vapi yogas described in stanza 5 as well as the Yupa, Ishu, Sakti and Danda yogas described in stanza 7 shall not be confounded with the Kedara yogas described in this stanza. And so on.
passages.summary: The text says that when a Sankhya (number-of-signs) yoga is also another Nabhasa yoga, it is to be classed as the other yoga.

passages.text: A person born under a Rajju yoga will be jealous of the wealth of others, will proceed to foreign lands and will be fond of travelling;
passages.notes: In this stanza, the author describes the effects of the three Asraya yogas and of the two Dala yogas.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Rajju yoga will envy others' wealth, go to foreign lands and love travel.

passages.text: a person born under a Musala yoga will be respectable, rich, and will engage in various undertakings ;
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Musala yoga will be respectable and rich and will take on various undertakings.

passages.text: and a person born under a Nala yoga will be of defective organs, settled views, rich and skilled in work.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Nala yoga will have defective organs and settled views, and will be rich and skilled in work.

passages.text: Again, a person born under a Srik yoga will live in comfort and luxury,
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Srik (Mala) yoga will live in comfort and luxury.

passages.text: and one born under a Sarpa yoga, will be miserable in many ways.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Sarpa yoga will be miserable in many ways.

passages.text: If the Asraya yogas partake at the same time of the character of other yogas they should be treated as the latter ; otherwise they produce the effects described for them.
passages.notes: This subject has already been discussed in stanza 3. For instance, if a Rajju yoga or a Musala yoga or a Nala yoga partake of the nature of a Kamala yoga (stanza 5) it should be treated as the latter.
passages.summary: The text says that when an Asraya yoga is also another yoga, it should be treated as the other yoga. Otherwise it gives its own stated effects.

passages.text: A person born under a Gada yoga will perform sacrificial rites, will be rich, and will ever be engaged in the acquisition of wealth;
passages.notes: In this stanza the author describes the effects of 5 Akriti yogas.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Gada yoga will perform sacrificial rites, be rich and always be occupied with acquiring wealth.

passages.text: a person born under a Sakata yoga will live by means of carts, will be afflicted with diseases, and will have a mean wife;
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Sakata yoga will earn a living by carts, suffer from diseases and have a mean wife.

passages.text: a person born under a Vihaga yoga will live by carrying messages, will be fond of travels, and will cause quarrels ;
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Vihaga yoga will earn a living by carrying messages, love travel and cause quarrels.

passages.text: a person born under a Sringataka yoga will be happy in the latter end of life (a)
passages.notes: (a). The word in the text is "Chira Sukha" This is interpreted by some to mean "happy for a long time." This interpretation is opposed to Garga.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Sringataka yoga will be happy in the later part of life.

passages.text: and a person born under a Hala yoga will till lands.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Hala yoga will farm the land.

passages.text: A person born under a Vajra yoga will be happy both at the beginning and end of life, will be a general favorite and will be bold in fight.
passages.notes: In this stanza, the author describes the effects of 4 more Akriti yogas.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Vajra yoga will be happy at the beginning and end of life, be liked by all and be bold in battle.

passages.text: A person born in a Yava yoga will be powerful, and will be happy at the middle of life.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Yava yoga will be powerful and happy in the middle of life.

passages.text: A person born under a Padma (Kamala) yoga will be of great renown, will be greatly happy and possessed of many attainments.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Padma (Kamala) yoga will be very famous, very happy and highly accomplished.

passages.text: A person born under a Vapi yoga will live in poor comfort for a long time, will bury his wealth under ground and will be a miser.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Vapi yoga will live in little comfort for a long time, bury his wealth underground and be a miser.

passages.text: A person born under a Yupa yoga will be liberal in gift and will perform high sacrificial rights.
passages.notes: In this stanza the author describes the effects of 4 more Akriti yogas.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Yupa yoga will be generous and will perform high sacrificial rites.

passages.text: A person born under a Bana (Ishu) yoga will indulge in torture, will be a jailor and will make arrows.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Bana (Ishu) yoga will indulge in torture, be a jailer and make arrows.

passages.text: A person born under a Sakti yoga will engage in deeds disgraceful to his rank in life, will not be skilled in work, and will be without money and comfort.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Sakti yoga will do things disgraceful to his rank, lack skill in work, and be without money and comfort.

passages.text: A person born under a Danda yoga will be separated from persons of his affection (a) and will earn his livelihood by the lowest of means, viz., servitude.
passages.notes: (a). Sons and the like.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Danda yoga will be separated from those he loves, such as sons, and will earn a living by servitude.

passages.text: A person born under a Nau yoga will be of wide-spread fame, happy only now and then, and will be a miser.
passages.notes: The effects of 4 more Akriti yogas are described in this stanza.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Nau yoga will be widely famous, happy only now and then, and a miser.

passages.text: A person born under a Kuta yoga will indulge in lies, and will be a jailor.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Kuta yoga will tell lies and be a jailer.

passages.text: A person born under a Chhatra yoga will make his people happy and will live in comfort in the latter end of life.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Chhatra yoga will make his people happy and live in comfort in the later part of life.

passages.text: A person born under a Chapa yoga will delight in fight and will live in comfort both at the beginning and end of life.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Chapa yoga will enjoy fighting and live in comfort at the beginning and end of life.

passages.text: A person born under an Ardha-Chandra yoga will be a general favorite, of agreeable person and be respected by all.
passages.notes: In this stanza the author describes the effects of the three Akriti yogas and of the first Sankhya yoga.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Ardha-Chandra yoga will be liked by all, pleasant in appearance and respected by everyone.

passages.text: A person born under a Samudra yoga will be as prosperous as a king and will live in comfort.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Samudra yoga will be as prosperous as a king and live in comfort.

passages.text: A person born under a Chakra yoga will have his feet illumined by the lustre of the gems in the crowns of kings falling prostrate before him by way of respect and submission (a).
passages.notes: (a). In other words he will become an emperor or king of kings.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Chakra yoga will have kings bowing at his feet in submission. The note explains this as becoming an emperor.

passages.text: A person born in a Vallaki yoga will be skilled in work and will delight in music and dance.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Vallaki yoga will be skilled in work and delight in music and dance.

passages.text: A person born under a Damini yoga will be liberal in gift, will delight in helping others and will possess many cows.
passages.notes: In this stanza the author describes the effects of 4 more Sankhya yogas.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Damini yoga will be generous, enjoy helping others and own many cows.

passages.text: A person born in a Pasa yoga will, with his servants and kinsmen, earn wealth by proper means.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Pasa yoga will earn wealth by proper means together with his servants and relatives.

passages.text: A person born under a Kedara yoga will till lands, and by doing good deeds, will be useful to others.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Kedara yoga will farm the land and be useful to others through good deeds.

passages.text: A person born under a Sula yoga will be bold in fight, will receive blows and will be fond of money (a) but will be poor.
passages.notes: (a). "Will be fond of torture" according to some other reading.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Sula yoga will be bold in battle, receive blows and love money, yet be poor. Another reading has him fond of torture.
passages.withheldReason: Predicts injury and violence (receiving blows, torture).

passages.text: A person born under a Yuga yoga will be poor and will act in contravention of Vedic rules.
passages.notes: In this stanza the effects of the remaining two Sankhya yogas are described.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Yuga yoga will be poor and will act against Vedic rules.

passages.text: A person born under a Gola yoga will be poor, dirty, ignorant, addicted to low deeds, unskilled in work, and will ever be wandering from place to place (a).
passages.notes: (a). For bare subsistence, according to commentator.
passages.summary: The text says a person born under Gola yoga will be poor, dirty, ignorant, given to low deeds and unskilled. It says he will always wander from place to place, which the commentator explains as seeking bare subsistence.

passages.text: Thus have been been described the several Nabhasa yogas with their effects. These effects are felt throughout a man's life.
passages.notes: (b). Except in the case of Vajra and other yogas (vide stanza 14) whose effects will be felt, as stated, in particular periods of a person's life. So that wherever no periods are mentioned the effects will be felt throughout life.
passages.summary: The text says this completes the Nabhasa yogas and their effects, and that these effects last throughout life. The note excepts yogas such as Vajra, whose effects are tied to particular periods of life.

passages.text: Dala Yogas will coincide neither with Asraya yogas nor with Akriti yogas. They might coincide with Sankhya yogas — with the Vallaki, the Damini, the Pasa, or the Kedara yogas, in which case the yogas are to be treated as only Dala yogas and not as Sankhya yogas. (Vide stanza 10). Again, according to stanza 12 if the Asraya yogas coincide with other yogas, they cease to be Asraya yogas and according to stanza 10 if the Sankhya yogas coincide with other yogas, they cease to be Sankhya yogas. Now suppose Asraya and Sankhya yogas to coincide with each other. Are they to be treated as the former or as the latter ? The commentator says that if the coincidence refers to the Kedara, Sula, and Yuga yogas, the yogas are to be treated as Asraya yogas only ; but if it refer to the Gola yoga, it is to be treated as such and not as an Asraya yoga — otherwise there will be no room for Gola yoga at all.
passages.summary: The translator's note explains how to classify overlapping Nabhasa yogas: Dala yogas take precedence over coinciding Sankhya yogas. Citing the commentator, it says Asraya yogas take precedence over Kedara, Sula and Yuga, but Gola stays Gola.

passages.text:
We shall now explain how the Yavanas obtain 1800 Nabhasa yogas. As stated in stanza 3, the Yavanas do not treat of the three Asraya yogas and the two Dala yogas. They treat of 23 Akriti yogas and 127 Sankhya yogas or 150 yogas in all for a Lagna ; there being 12 Lagnas, the number of Nabhasa yogas treated of by the Yavanas is 12x150=1800.
We shall explain these more fully. As explained in note (a) to stanza 4, the Gada yoga of the author is treated of as 4 distinct yogas by the Yavanas. Adding these to the remaining 19 Akriti yogas, we get 23 Akriti yogas as treated of by the Yavanas.
Again, the seven Sankhya yogas of the author are split into 127 Sankhya yogas (for a Lagna) by the Yavanas as follows : The first Sankhya yoga treated of by Varaha Mihira is known as Vallaki yoga according to which the 7 planets might occupy any seven signs. This may be in many ways ; but the Yavanas select only a few : as each of the seven planets might occupy the Lagna the number of yogas under this division is 7. Again the 2nd Sankhya yoga treated of by the author is one according to which the 7 planets are said to occupy any six signs. This may be in many ways ; but the Yavanas select the following few : of the 7 planets 5 may occupy 5 houses and two more may occupy the Lagna. These two may be any two of the seven planets. The number of yogas under this head will be the number of combinations of 7 things taken 2 together =7/1x6/2=21.
Again, the 3rd Sankhya yoga is one in which the seven planets occupy 5 houses. This may be in many ways ; but the following are selected: — 4 planets occupying 4 houses and 3 more occupying the Lagna. These three may be any three out of the 7 planets. The number of cases under this head is the number of combinations of 7 things taken 3 together =7/1x6/2x5/3=35.
The next Sankhya yoga of Varaha Mihira is similarly split by the Yavanas into 7/1x6/2x5/3x4/4=35, and the next into 7/1x6/2x5/3x4/4x3/5=21, and the next into 7/1x6/2x5/3x4/4x3/5x2/6=7, and the last into 7/1x6/2x5/3x4/4x3/5x2/6x1/7=1. So that the seven Sankhya yogas are split into 7+21+35+35+21+7+1=127. These added to 23 Akriti yogas give us 150 yogas for a Lagna or 1800 yogas for the 12 Lagnas.
To find the number of combinations of n things taken r at a time, the reader is referred to the Lilavati of Bhaskara Charyar or to the Chhandas Sutra of Pingala or to Chapter 77, stanza 22 (notes) of the English Translation of Brihat Samhita or to the notes to stanza 4 of the next Chapter of this Book.
passages.summary: The translator's note shows how the Yavanas reach 1,800 Nabhasa yogas: 23 Akriti yogas plus 127 Sankhya variants make 150 per ascendant, multiplied by 12 ascendants. It only counts and classifies yogas.

passages.text: The conduct, wealth, knowledge, intelligence and skill of a person will be poor, moderate or excellent according as the Moon occupies the Kendra, the Panaphara or the Apoklima houses from the Sun (a),
passages.notes: (a). At the time of birth. In other words, a person will have very little of these qualities if the Moon occupy either the sign occupied by the Sun or the 4th, 7th or 10th sign from it. He will have these qualities in a moderate degree if the Moon occupy the 2nd, 5th, 8th or 11th sign from the sign occupied by the Sun ; and he will have these qualities in a large measure, if the Moon occupy the 3rd, 6th, 9th or 12th sign from the sign occupied by the Sun.
passages.summary: The text says a person's conduct, wealth, knowledge, intelligence and skill will be poor, moderate or excellent according as the Moon stands in an angular, succedent or cadent house counted from the Sun.

passages.text: a person will be rich and will live in comfort if the Moon occupy his own Navamsa or an Atimitra Navamsa (b), provided she is aspected by Jupiter if the birth occur by day, and by Venus if the birth occur by night.
passages.notes: (b). An Atimitra Navamsa is a Navamsa of an Atimitra or a very friendly planet.
passages.summary: The text says a person will be rich and live in comfort if the Moon is in her own Navamsa or the Navamsa of a very friendly planet, provided she is aspected by Jupiter in a day birth or by Venus in a night birth.

passages.text: If the benefic planets (a) occupy the 6th, 7th and 8th houses from the Moon, the yoga is known as Adhi-yoga (b). A person born in the yoga will become a general, a minister or a king (c) and will be in the enjoyment of great pleasures and wealth with subdued enemies and long life and free from diseases and fear.
passages.notes:
(a). These are Mercury, Jupiter and Venus.
(b). The yoga is of 7 sorts according as the benefic planets occupy one or more of the three houses : (1), They might occupy all the three houses ; (2), or the 6th and 7th houses ; (3) or the 6th and 8th ; (4) the 7th and 8th, (5), the 6th ; (6) the 7th ; (7), the 8th houses from the Moon.
(c). According as Mercury, Jupiter and Venus are weak, of moderate power, or of very great power according to Badarayana.
passages.summary: The text says that when the benefic planets occupy the 6th, 7th and 8th houses from the Moon, the Adhi yoga is formed, and the person becomes a general, a minister or a king, enjoys great pleasures and wealth, subdues enemies, and lives long free from disease and fear.

passages.text: In the Astrological work known as Saravali, the Adhi yoga is classed with Raja yoga when the planets Mercury, Jupiter and Venus are not Astangata planets, nor aspected by malefic planets. Mandavya is of the same opinion.
passages.summary: The translator's note says that the Saravali, and Mandavya likewise, class the Adhi yoga as a Raja yoga when Mercury, Jupiter and Venus are not combust and not aspected by malefic planets.

passages.text: Excepting the Sun if the other planets occupy the 2nd, the 12th, or both the 2nd and the 12th houses from the Moon, the yoga is respectively known as Sunapha, Anapha or Durudhura ;
passages.summary: The text defines the Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhura yogas: planets other than the Sun in the 2nd house from the Moon, in the 12th house from the Moon, or in both, respectively.

passages.text: otherwise (a), the yoga is known as Kemadruma by numerous writers.
passages.notes: (a). Otherwise : i. e., if the 2nd, the 12th, or both the 2nd and the 12th houses from the Moon be not occupied by planets — the Sun excepted.
passages.summary: The text says that when no planet other than the Sun occupies the 2nd or 12th house from the Moon, numerous writers call the yoga Kemadruma.

passages.text: According to some (b), if the Moon occupy the Kendra house from the ascendant or if the Moon be accompanied by a planet, the yoga ceases to be a Kemadruma yoga.
passages.notes: (b). Garga and Parasara.
passages.summary: According to some authorities (Garga and Parasara, per the note), the yoga ceases to be Kemadruma if the Moon is in an angular house from the ascendant or is accompanied by a planet.

passages.text: According to others (c) the three yogas, Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhura are referred to the Kendra houses from the Moon (d),
passages.notes:
(c). Srutakeerti and others.
(d). That is, if the planets excepting the Sun occupy the 4th house from the Moon, the yoga is known as Sunapha; if they occupy the 10th house from the Moon, the yoga is known as Anapha, and if they occupy both the 4th and the 10th house from the Moon, it is known as Durudhura and if the 4th and 10th houses from the Moon be not occupied by planets, the yoga is known as Kemadruma.
passages.summary: According to other writers (Srutakeerti and others, per the note), the Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhura yogas are reckoned from the 4th and 10th houses from the Moon instead.

passages.text: while again some others (e) refer the three yogas to the houses on both sides of the sign the Navamsa of which the Moon occupies (f). But these views are not considered as authoritative.
passages.notes:
(e). Jeevasarma.
(f). Suppose the Moon to occupy the Navamsa of Sagittari in sign Aries. Now if the planets, excepting the Sun and the Moon occupy the 2nd, or the 12th or both the 2nd and the 12th houses from sign Sagittari the yoga is respectively known as Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhura. but if these two houses be not so occupied the yoga is known as Kemadruma.
passages.summary: The text says still others (Jeevasarma, per the note) reckon the three yogas from the signs on either side of the sign whose Navamsa the Moon occupies, and that these alternative views are not considered authoritative.

passages.text: The Sunapha and the Anapha yogas are each of thirty-one sorts,
passages.summary: The text says the Sunapha and Anapha yogas each come in thirty-one varieties; it only counts them.

passages.text: and the Durudhura yogas are of one hundred and eighty sorts, as will be found to be the case by forming series as described in the rule for finding the number of combinations of a given number of things.
passages.summary: The text says the Durudhura yogas come in one hundred and eighty varieties, found by the rule for counting combinations; it only counts them.

passages.text: The rule for finding the number of combinations of a given number of things is only hinted at in the text, but not fully given. It is quoted in stanza 22 of Chapter 79 of the Brihat Samhita. The rule is: — "Beginning from unity, form a series by adding together the first figure with the next and the sum with the next figure and so on omitting only the last. From the series thus formed, form a fresh series similarly, beginning from unity, and so on. The last terms of the several series will give the number of combinations required." Suppose there to be 7 substances. The figures 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, will form the first series. Obtain the 2nd series as follows: 1+2=3; 3+3=6; 6+4=10; 10+5=15; 15+6=21. The 2nd series therefore is 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21. Obtain the 3rd series as follows: 1+3=4; 4+6=10; 10+10=20; 20+15=35. The 3rd series therefore is 1, 4, 10, 20, 35. Obtain the 4th series as follows : 1+4=5; 5+10=15; 15+20=35. The 4th series therefore is 1, 5, 15, 35. Obtain the 5th series as follows: 1+5=6. 6+15=21. The 5th series therefore is 1, 6, 21. Obtain the 6th series as follows : 1+6=7. The 6th series therefore is 1, 7. The seventh series is 1. The last terms of the seven series are, 7, 21, 35, 35, 21, 7, 1. These are respectively the number of combinations of seven things taken 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 at a time. Bhaskara Chariar gives a simpler process in his Lilavati—a work on Arithmetic. He says : Form fractions with the numbers beginning from the last number to unity for numerators and with the numbers beginning from unity to the last number for denominators respectively. The number of combinations taken 1, 2, 3, 4, &c., at a time will respectively be the first fraction, the product of 1st two fractions, of the first three fractions or of the 1st four fractions, &c. Suppose, for instance, the number of things to be 7. Then the fractions are 7/1, 6/2, 5/3, 4/4, 3/5, 2/6, 1/7. The number of combinations of 7 things taken one at a time=7/1=7 ; Taken two at a time=7/1×6/2=21, taken 3 at a time=7/1×6/2×5/3=35 ; taken 4 at a time=7/1×6/2×5/3×4/4=35; taken 5 at a time=7/1×6/2×5/3×4/4×3/5=21 ; taken 6 at a time=7/1×6/2×5/3×4/4×3/5×2/6=7; and taken 7 at a time=7/1×6/2×5/3×4/4×3/5×2/6×1/7=1.
passages.summary: The translator's note sets out the rule, quoted from the Brihat Samhita and from Bhaskara's Lilavati, for counting the combinations of a number of things, worked through for seven things. It concerns arithmetic only and states no astrological results.

passages.text: Now in the Sunapha or Anapha yogas the 2nd or the 12th house from the Moon may be occupied by the five planets from Mars either singly or two at a time or three or four or all at a time. The number required is the number of combinations of five things taken 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 together at a time. This is to be deduced from the following : 5/1, 4/2, 3/3, 2/4, 1/5. The number will be found to be 5+10+10+5+1=31.
passages.summary: The translator's note works out that the Sunapha and Anapha yogas each have 31 varieties, since any one to five of the five planets from Mars onward may occupy the 2nd or 12th house from the Moon. It only counts the varieties.

passages.text: Take the case in which the 2nd house from the Moon is occupied by a single planet; while it does so, the remaining four planets may occupy the 12th house from the Moon 1, 2, 3 and 4 at a time. The number of these will be the sum of the number of combinations of four things taken 1, 2, 3 and 4 together. This will be found to be 4+6+4+1=15. So that for one of the five Sunapha yogas we get 15 Durudhura yogas. The five Sunapha yogas of one planet will therefore give us 5×15=75 Durudhura yogas. Take one of the 10 Sunapha yogas of two planets from Mars to Saturn ; the remaining 3 planets may occupy the 12th house from the Moon, 1, 2 and 3 at a time. The number required is the sum of the number of combinations of three things taken 1, 2 and 3 at a time. This will be found to be 3+3+1=7. Combining these with the 10 Sunapha yogas of 2 planets we shall get 10×7=70 Durudhura yogas. Similarly the 10 Sunapha yogas of three planets will give 10×3=30 Durudhura yogas; and the five Sunapha yogas of 4 planets will give us 5×1=5 Durudhura yogas. So that the number of possible Durudhura yogas=75+70+30+5=180.
passages.summary: The translator's note works out that there are 180 possible Durudhura yogas by counting how the remaining planets can fill the 12th house from the Moon for each arrangement in the 2nd house. It only counts the varieties.

passages.text: A person born in a Sunapha yoga will be possessed of self-acquired property, will be a king or will resemble a king, and will be a man of intelligence, wealth and renown.
passages.summary: The text says a person born in Sunapha yoga will have self-acquired property, will be a king or like a king, and will be intelligent, wealthy and renowned.

passages.text: A person born in an Anapha yoga will be a man of influence and authority, will be free from diseases, will have a control over his passions, will be of great renown, will be in the enjoyment of all manner of pleasures, will wear neat dress and will be free from grief.
passages.summary: The text says a person born in Anapha yoga will have influence and authority, be free from disease, control his passions, be greatly renowned, enjoy all kinds of pleasures, dress neatly and be free from grief.

passages.text: A person born in a Durudhura yoga will be in the enjoyment of all manner of pleasures, will be possessed of wealth and chariot, will be liberal in his gifts and will have good servants.
passages.summary: The text says a person born in Durudhura yoga will enjoy all kinds of pleasures, own wealth and a chariot, give generously and have good servants.

passages.text: A person born in a Kemadruma yoga, though he may belong to a king's family, will be dirty, afflicted with grief, will do deeds not suited to his rank in life, will be poor, will serve under others and will be wicked.
passages.summary: The text says a person born in Kemadruma yoga, even if of royal family, will be dirty, grief-stricken, act beneath his rank, be poor, serve others and be wicked.

passages.text: If the yoga planet be Mars, the person will be active, fond of fight and wealthy, and will engage in deeds without thought.
passages.summary: The text says that if Mars is the planet forming the yoga, the person will be active, fond of fighting, wealthy, and will act without thinking.

passages.text: If the yoga planet be Mercury, the person will be skilled in work, will be of good speech and learned in the arts (a).
passages.notes: (a). In music, dance, painting, &c.
passages.summary: The text says that if Mercury is the planet forming the yoga, the person will be skilled in work, well-spoken and learned in the arts.

passages.text: If the yoga planet be Jupiter, a person will be wealthy and virtuous, will live for ever in comfort and will be respected by the king.
passages.summary: The text says that if Jupiter is the planet forming the yoga, the person will be wealthy and virtuous, always live in comfort and be respected by the king.

passages.text: If the yoga planet be Venus, a person will be afflicted with sexual passion, will be very wealthy and in the enjoyment of all manner of pleasures.
passages.summary: The text says that if Venus is the planet forming the yoga, the person will be afflicted with sexual passion, very wealthy and will enjoy all kinds of pleasures.

passages.text: If the yoga planet be Saturn, a person will enjoy the wealth, property and servants of others, will engage in various deeds and will be the chief of parties of men (a).
passages.notes: (a). If two or more planets be yoga planets the effects described for them all will come to pass.
passages.summary: The text says that if Saturn is the planet forming the yoga, the person will enjoy others' wealth, property and servants, undertake various deeds and lead groups of men. The note adds that when several planets form the yoga, all their effects occur.

passages.text: If the birth occur by day, the Moon will bring on misery if she occupy the visible hemisphere, and will bring on prosperity if she occupy the invisible hemisphere ; if otherwise, the results will be the reverse of these (b).
passages.notes: (b). That is, if the birth occur by night, the Moon will bring on misery if she occupy the invisible hemisphere and prosperity if she occupy the visible hemisphere.
passages.summary: The text says that in a day birth the Moon brings misery when above the horizon and prosperity when below it, and in a night birth the reverse.

passages.text: If all the benefic planets (a) occupy the Upachaya places (b) from the ascendant at the time of birth, a person will be very rich and if they occupy the Upachaya places from the Moon, he will be moderately rich. If two of the planets occupy the Upachaya places a person will be moderately wealthy and if one of them occupy such places he will possess small wealth (c). Even if the person be born in other malefic Yogas (d) the present yoga will take effect to their exclusion (e).
passages.notes:
(a). Mercury, Jupiter and Venus.
(b). The 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th houses from the ascendant.
(c). Or poor. If benefic planets occupy the Upachaya places both from the ascendant and from the Moon a person will be exceedingly rich.
(d). Such as Kemadruma yoga.
(e). That is, suppose a person to be born in a Kemadruma yoga and suppose the benefic planets to occupy the Upachaya places from the ascendant or the Moon or both, the person will become rich and not poor.
passages.summary: The text says that if all the benefic planets occupy the 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th houses from the ascendant the person will be very rich, and moderately rich if from the Moon; two such planets give moderate wealth and one gives small wealth. It adds that this yoga takes effect even over other malefic yogas such as Kemadruma.

passages.text: If at the time of birth the Sun and the Moon occupy together a sign of the Zodiac, the person born will be a maker of fire engines (a) and will work in stones;
passages.notes: (a). Engines of destruction according to Commentator.
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Sun and the Moon together in one sign will make fire engines and work in stones. The translator's footnote says the commentator takes these as engines of destruction.

passages.text: if the Sun and Mars occupy a sign together, the person will be addicted to sinful deeds;
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Sun and Mars together in one sign will be given to sinful deeds.

passages.text: if the Sun and Mercury occupy a sign together, the person will be skilled in work, will be intelligent and famous, and will live in comfort;
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Sun and Mercury together in one sign will be skilled in work, intelligent and famous, and will live in comfort.

passages.text: if the Sun and Jupiter occupy a sign together, the person will be cruel and will work for other men;
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Sun and Jupiter together in one sign will be cruel and will work for others.

passages.text: if the Sun and Venus occupy a sign together the person will gain money by engaging in public sports and by the use of weapons,
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Sun and Venus together in one sign will earn money through public sports and the use of weapons.

passages.text: and if the Sun and Saturn occupy a sign together, the person will be skilled in metal work and in earthen-ware.
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Sun and Saturn together in one sign will be skilled in metal work and earthenware.

passages.text: If the double planets occupying together a sign of the Zodiac at the time of birth be the Moon and Mars the person will earn money by the sale of works of art, of women, of liquor, and of pots and will give trouble to his mother;
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Moon and Mars together in one sign will earn money by selling works of art, women, liquor and pots, and will trouble his mother.
passages.withheldReason: Trade in women; harm to mother.

passages.text: [If the double planets occupying together a sign of the Zodiac at the time of birth be] the Moon and Mercury, the person will be of sweet speech, skilled in literary interpretation and will become popular and famous;
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Moon and Mercury together in one sign will speak sweetly, be skilled in literary interpretation, and become popular and famous.

passages.text: [If the double planets occupying together a sign of the Zodiac at the time of birth be] the Moon and Jupiter, the person will defeat his enemies, will be an important person in his family, will not be of firm views and will be greatly rich;
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Moon and Jupiter together in one sign will defeat his enemies, be important in his family, lack firm views, and be very rich.

passages.text: [If the double planets occupying together a sign of the Zodiac at the time of birth be] the Moon and Venus, the person will be skilled in cloth work (a);
passages.notes: (a). In weaving, stitching, dyeing, buying and selling cloths.
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Moon and Venus together in one sign will be skilled in cloth work, which the translator explains as weaving, stitching, dyeing and trading in cloth.

passages.text: [If the double planets occupying together a sign of the Zodiac at the time of birth be] the Moon and Saturn, the person will be the son of a re-married woman (b).
passages.notes: (b). The Sanscrit term for the woman is Punarbhu. She is said to be a woman, who, out of sexual passion, quits her husband and marries a person of her own caste whether or not she may have joined in sexual union.
passages.summary: The text says that a person born with the Moon and Saturn together in one sign will be the son of a remarried woman; the translator's footnote explains the Sanskrit term for such a woman.
passages.withheldReason: Low social birth; sexual immorality of mother.
